title: Algorithms to Live By: The Computer Science of Human Decisions
reason: After 20+ years publishing in behavioral economics I've read Kahneman forward and backward. What I do NOT have is a rigorous treatment of how computer-science algorithms — optimal stopping, explore/exploit trade-offs, caching — map onto human decision-making. That's precisely the novel angle this book offers. It reframes my own domain through a completely different lens, which is exactly what I look for now that I'm retired and running a small business where I actually have to make those decisions myself, not just model them. The cross-disciplinary novelty earns it a spot on my shelf.
